entries.title: HKEX Calendar
entries.publisher: Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited
entries.notes: The exchange's own calendar. Each Hong Kong general holiday appears with the description "Hong Kong Market is closed"; each shortened session appears as "Half-Day Trading Day - Afternoon Session is Closed on Christmas's Eve / New Year's Eve / Lunar New Year's Eve". The page embeds its data as a `calendarDataSource` JSON blob covering roughly one year either side of the retrieval date.

entries.title: HKEX Calendar (archived captures)
entries.publisher: Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited, via the Internet Archive
entries.notes: Same page, same embedded `calendarDataSource` format, read out of archived captures so that the exchange's own holiday and half-day entries could be checked for every year of coverage rather than only the live window. Every closure it lists for 2018-2027 agrees exactly with the gazetted general holidays list; no closure appears in one and not the other.

entries.title: Trading Hours - Securities Market
entries.publisher: Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited
entries.notes: "Trading is conducted on Monday to Friday (excluding public holidays)". Full day: 09:30-12:00 morning, 12:00-13:00 extended morning, 13:00-16:00 afternoon, closing auction 16:00 to a random close. Half day: morning session only, closing auction "12:00 noon to a random closing between 12:08 p.m. and 12:10 p.m.". Note: "There is no Extended Morning Session and Afternoon Session on the eves of Christmas, New Year and Lunar New Year." This is the source for the recurring half-day rule and for the 12:00 close time.

entries.title: Trading Calendar and Holiday Schedule (derivatives market)
entries.publisher: Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited
entries.notes: HKFE's holiday table for 2026 and 2027, listing the same Hong Kong general holidays that close the securities market, plus the notes naming the shortened sessions: "16 February 2026 (Monday) - Eve of Lunar New Year", "24 December 2026 (Thursday) - Eve of Christmas Day", "31 December 2026 (Thursday) - Eve of New Year", "05 February 2027 (Friday) - Eve of Lunar New Year", "24 December 2027 (Friday) - Eve of Christmas Day", "31 December 2027 (Friday) - Eve of New Year". Used to confirm the two 2027 December eves, which fall past the live HKEX Calendar window.

entries.title: Trading Calendar of Stock Connect (annual PDFs)
entries.publisher: Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited
entries.notes: Per-year grid marking each Hong Kong trading day "Holiday" or "Half Day". Used as a second HKEX publication corroborating the closures and half days already taken from `hkex-calendar`; it introduced no date of its own.

entries.title: General Holidays (per-year lists)
entries.publisher: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government
entries.notes: The Government's published list of general holidays for each year, as gazetted under the General Holidays Ordinance (Cap. 149). Each row gives the holiday's statutory name, date and weekday, already carrying any substitution ("the day following ...", "the fourth day of Lunar New Year", "the second weekday after Christmas Day"). Only the current and next few years stay online; 2028 was not yet published at the retrieval date.

entries.title: General Holidays (per-year lists, archived captures)
entries.publisher: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government, via the Internet Archive
entries.notes: The same per-year gov.hk pages for years the Government has since taken down, read from mid-year captures (by which point the year's list is final). Table shape and wording are identical to the live pages; the weekday named in each row was checked against the date as a transcription guard.

entries.title: Gregorian-Lunar Calendar Conversion Table
entries.publisher: Hong Kong Observatory, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government
entries.covers: 1901-2100; all 2016-2029 annual tables and selected boundary/uncertainty tables retained locally
entries.notes: Authority for the published Hong Kong Gregorian/lunar correspondences and Bright & Clear solar-term rows. HKO and the gazetted HK schedule start the 2027 lunar year on 6 February; pinned ICU4J 78.3 starts it on 7 February, so the calendar carries authoritative replacement rows. HKO also warns that new moons close to midnight can differ by one day in 2057, 2089 and 2097. ICU differs from HKO at 2057-09-28 (HKO M09 day 1; ICU M08 day 30 and M09 begins 2057-09-29), while agreeing on the checked 2089 and 2097 rows. Disputed future conversions are not treated as verified exchange schedules.

entries.title: Securities and Derivatives Market Trading Arrangements under Typhoon Signal No. 8 (Market Communications)
entries.publisher: Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited
entries.notes: Example of a same-day severe-weather announcement (the 06 September 2024 morning notice): "trading of its securities ... and derivatives markets today (Friday) has been impacted by the issuance of Typhoon Signal No.8 ... If Typhoon Signal No. 8 or above, Black Rainstorm Warning or any announcement of Extreme Conditions, remains issued at 12:00 noon, all trading sessions today will be cancelled." Shows the mechanism: the session is cancelled on the day, by announcement. The dated closures themselves cite the individual hkex-no-trading-<date> notices; see the severe-weather section below.

entries.title: Hong Kong Public Holidays iCal / JSON feed
entries.publisher: 1823, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government
entries.notes: The Government's machine-readable feed of the same gazetted general holidays, linked from the gov.hk holiday pages. Used as an independent transcription check on 2025-2027; it matched the HTML pages row for row.

entries.title: HKEX to Implement Severe Weather Trading in Securities and Derivatives Markets from 23 September 2024
entries.publisher: Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited
entries.notes: HKEX states that its securities and derivatives markets remain open and operational during severe weather under the arrangements effective 23 September 2024.

entries.title: Warnings and Signals Database: tropical cyclone warning signals (tc.dat) and rainstorm warning signals (rstorm.dat)
entries.publisher: Hong Kong Observatory
entries.notes: The Observatory's complete record of every Tropical Cyclone Warning Signal and Rainstorm Warning Signal with issue and cancellation times (HKT). Every HKEX severe-weather closure before 23 September 2024 required a Signal No. 8 or above, a Black Rainstorm Warning or an Extreme Conditions announcement, so enumerating every such record over the period and applying the exchange's published arrangements (hkex-severe-weather-arrangements-2023) bounds the set of trading days that could have been affected. All T8+ and Black records 2018-2024 are reproduced in the prose below; each one maps either to an HKEX notice or to a weekend, holiday, out-of-session or before-07:00 cancellation that left trading as usual.

entries.title: Severe Weather Arrangements - Trading (securities market tables (a)-(d), archived)
entries.publisher: Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited
entries.notes: The pre-SWT rules: a signal/warning "discontinued at or before 7:00 am: Trading will take place as usual"; "discontinued after 9:00 am and at or before 11:00 am: The Pre-opening Session and the Morning Session will be cancelled. The Afternoon Session will take place as usual at 1:00 pm"; "discontinued after 12:00 noon: No trading for the day"; a T8 issued during a session: "Trading will terminate 15 minutes after the issuance of the signal"; a Black Rainstorm issued during a session: "trading will continue until the market close as scheduled". The same wording appears verbatim in every HKEX delay notice 2019-2024.

entries.title: Consultation Paper on Severe Weather Trading of Hong Kong Securities and Derivatives Markets (November 2023)
entries.publisher: Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited
entries.notes: Independent count used as a cross-check: "Since 2018, SW conditions have forced market closures on 11 occasions" and the markets were "impacted by SW a total of four times in 2023, including three full-day market suspensions". The eleven dated disruptions modelled here through 9 October 2023 (2019: 1, 2020: 2, 2021: 2, 2022: 2, 2023: 4 of which 3 whole days) match that count exactly. Paragraph 88 also fixes the business-day meaning: only an entire-day closure means SEHK is not "open for the business of dealing in securities"; a half-day closure remains a business day.

entries.title: Trading in Securities and Derivatives Markets Terminated Due to Issuance of Typhoon Signal No. 8 (Tropical Storm Wipha)
entries.publisher: Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited
entries.notes: HKEX market communication of 31 July 2019: "trading in the securities market, including Stock Connect trading, and derivatives markets will be terminated at 1:55pm". Signal No. 8 was issued at 13:40 (hko-warnings-database); the morning session traded in full, the afternoon session closed at 13:55 with no Closing Auction Session. Modelled as an EARLY_CLOSE at 13:55; the date remains a business day.

"There will be no After-Hours Trading session today." Signal No. 8 was issued at 13:40 (hko-warnings-database); modelled as an EARLY_CLOSE at 13:55; the date remains a business day.

entries.title: Trading in Securities and Derivatives Markets will Resume (Severe Tropical Storm Higos)
entries.publisher: Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited
entries.notes: HKEX market communication of 2020-08-19: "trading in the securities and derivatives markets will resume at 1:30pm ... there will be no Pre-opening Session". The Pre-opening and Morning Sessions were cancelled and the afternoon session traded to the scheduled close. A late open is not an event in this model (session structure is out of scope), so the date is an ordinary business day with no row; the notice is cited so the absence of a closure is evidenced rather than assumed.
